entries.title: Sharp Bounds for Graph Matrices

entries.abstract: An explicit construction of 23 distinct points and 23 distinct straight lines in the real affine plane, with exactly four selected incidences at every point and every line. Lean verifies the construction using rational coordinates interpreted in the real numbers.
entries.title: A real affine (23_4) configuration

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 from the paper "Power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions" by Marco Fraccaroli, Joris Roos, and Andreas Seeger, arXiv:2602.17613. The formalized result concerns boundedness of  spherical maximal functions with arbitrary sets of dilations and radial power weights. The allowable exponent and weight ranges are characterized, apart from endpoint boundedness, by the Legendre-Assouad function of the dilation set. This resolved an open problem of Duoandikoetxea and Seijo up to endpoints. The main theorem statement in Lean was human-generated, while the formal proofs where machine-generated by coding agents under human supervision following the mathematical source directly.
entries.title: Formalization of power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the Erdős–Rado negative stepping-up lemma in its order-type form, for arities three and above and for at least two colours.
Fix an ordinal kappa; a colour count mu ≥ 2; and a target order type theta = omega^alpha with alpha > 0, so that theta is additively indecomposable. The theorem proved is, for every natural number r: if some colouring of the (r+3)-subsets of kappa by ordinals below mu admits no monochromatic subset of kappa of order type theta, then some colouring of the (r+4)-subsets of 2^kappa admits none either, using the same number of colours.
The construction compares two unrelated orders on 2^kappa -- an arbitrary well-order, and the lexicographic order given by the first place two sets differ -- and reads a colouring off the pattern of agreement between them along a chain, together with the sequence of discrepancies. Two colours are spent marking the chains where those patterns first deviate, and on the well-behaved chains the colouring copies the given one along the discrepancy map.
entries.title: Erdős–Rado negative stepping-up for ordinal order types

entries.abstract: For finite nonempty action sets and unit-interval full-information payoffs, regret matching and regret matching+ have cumulative external regret at most the square root of the product of the number of actions and the horizon, against every fixed pure or mixed comparator. In finite two-player zero-sum matrix games, simultaneous self-play gives an explicit finite-time approximate Nash guarantee for uniformly averaged strategies. A finite-vector implementation is proved to reproduce the abstract averages. Square-root-free accuracy budgets and finite rational payoff inequalities certify approximate equilibria, including against all real mixed deviations. A four-round rational RM+ example has certified Nash error at most 19/260.
entries.title: Verified regret matching and finite-time equilibrium computation

entries.abstract: For finite games with player-specific action types, a valid independent product distribution is a correlated equilibrium exactly when its mixed profile is Nash. The correlated-equilibrium set is nonempty, compact, and convex when every player's action type is nonempty. For every positive finite horizon, cumulative external-regret and swap-regret bounds give corresponding approximate coarse-correlated and correlated equilibria of the empirical distribution. The development also proves equivalence with conditional obedience inequalities, arbitrary mixed-deviation sufficiency, and extension-by-zero correspondence for restricted legal actions. An exact per-recommendation certificate characterizes approximate correlated equilibrium without loss in its error budget and directly certifies empirical play from cumulative recommendation gains.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Finite correlated equilibria and regret certificates

entries.abstract: Formalizes the quantitative almost-Schur lemma on nonempty connected closed smooth Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least three with nonnegative Ricci curvature: scalar-curvature variance is bounded by 4*n*(n-1)/(n-2)^2 times the squared L2 norm of trace-free Ricci, with the Einstein equality characterization. The development constructs normalized Riemannian volume, solves the mean-zero Poisson problem variationally and upgrades it to a smooth representative, proves the actual integrated Bochner and contracted-Bianchi identities, and closes the sharp algebra.

authors.name: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

entries.title: De Lellis--Topping almost-Schur inequality

entries.abstract: A Lean-native formalization of finite mixed Nash equilibrium for games in which each player has its own finite, nonempty action type. The library defines dependent profiles and finite expected payoffs, proves support equalization and Dirac transport, establishes the closed/compact/convex mixed-profile geometry, and connects the normalized excess map to a checked product-of-simplices Brouwer theorem. It also proves the correspondence between ambient finite games with player-indexed legal action sets and dependent legal-action subtypes. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics or priority.
entries.title: Dependent finite mixed Nash equilibria in Lean

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that for every nonnegative integer n, the distinct integers 1,...,n can be partitioned into nonempty sets of at most three elements, each having sum equal to a nonnegative integer power of three. This proves Conjecture 1 of Gurvich and Naumova, arXiv:2508.00946v3. The development constructs permutations with all prescribed nonzero displacements, derives signed zero-sum triple partitions, proves a contraction and complement-pair extension, and completes strong induction on n. All required finite certificates and unbounded sequence constructions are proved in Lean.
entries.title: gn-lean: the Gurvich–Naumova partition conjecture

entries.abstract: Let B(n) and A(n) be the integer solution sets of 2x^2 + y^2 + 8z^2 = n and 2u^2 + v^2 + 32w^2 = n, respectively. For every odd positive squarefree n satisfying |B(n)| = 2|A(n)|, we construct a deterministic computable map Phi_n : B(n) -> A(n) that sends exactly two source points to each target point. The construction combines an elementary even-coordinate map, three explicit quarter-turn correspondences, and a unique stable matching of the remaining antipodal orbits, with preferences determined by primitive midpoint directions. The map, its two-to-one property, the branch formulas, and the inverse identities for the residual map are formalized in Lean 4. Tunnell's theorem supplies the required counting identity for odd squarefree congruent numbers; its modular-form proof lies outside this formalization.
entries.title: A two-to-one executable map between Tunnell representation sets under the Tunnell balance

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization proving that the Moh curve parametrized by x=t^6+t^31, y=t^8, z=t^10 is cut out set-theoretically by two explicit equations over every characteristic-zero field. The development computes the polynomial and formal-power-series parametrization kernels, proves the radical equality for the two-generated witness ideal, and proves that the curve ideal has height two and arithmetic rank two, both globally and after completion.
entries.title: Moh's P3 curve is a set-theoretic complete intersection

entries.abstract: For n independent trials with success probabilities p_1, ..., p_n in [0,1] -- Poisson trials -- and S the number of successes, three results about how the law of S varies over all trial vectors with a given mean lam, with pbar = lam/n the common success probability of the homogeneous trials of the same mean. First, for g convex on the integer grid, E[g S] is maximised by the binomial, and under strict grid convexity equality holds exactly at the constant vector (Hoeffding's Theorem 3). Second, for arbitrary g with no convexity assumed, the maximum and the minimum of E[g S] over the fixed-mean box are attained at points whose coordinates take at most three distinct values, at most one of them strictly between 0 and 1 (Corollary 2.1). Third, away from the mean the binomial extremises the lower tail: for k >= lam the homogeneous vector has the lightest lower tail and for k <= lam - 1 the heaviest (two of the three regimes of Theorem 4). Every compared statement is written without any definition of its own: the probability model, the tail and the binomial comparator are expanded into raw Finset sums, products and filters from Mathlib, so that each claim can be audited against the informal statement without first accepting a definition.
entries.title: Hoeffding's extrema of the number of successes at a fixed mean

entries.abstract: Formalizes finite strategic-form games with player-specific finite move sets, pure profiles, unilateral deviations, best responses, dominant strategies, and two distinct potential notions. Pure Nash equilibrium is defined over utility preorders by the absence of a strict improvement; weak-inequality characterizations are restricted to linear orders. The library names the one-way improvement condition a generalized ordinal potential and reserves ordinal potential for the standard bidirectional strict-sign condition. It proves a global potential-maximizer certificate for pure Nash equilibrium, the standard Nash/local-potential-maximum equivalence, and acyclicity of the better-response relation for the generalized class. The development also gives checked counterexamples and Prisoner's-Dilemma/coordination/matching-pennies/rock-paper-scissors examples. Its native mixed layer proves support equalization, Dirac transport, the normalized excess-map reduction, and the closed/compact/ convex/continuous finite mixed-profile geometry. It also proves general finite mixed-Nash existence on a common nonempty move type by connecting the native excess map to an attributed, kernel-checked product-of-simplices Brouwer theorem. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics or the first Lean proof of Nash existence.
entries.title: Native Lean finite Nash equilibria

entries.abstract: A bound between all s-numbers (in the sense of Pietsch). The approximation  numbers a_n are the largest s-number sequence and the Hilbert numbers h_n  the smallest, so that h_n(S) <= s_n(S) <= a_n(S) holds for every s-number  sequence (s_n) and every bounded linear operator S between Banach spaces.  The formalized result gives a bound in the reverse direction:  a_n(S) <= ((n+1)^(n+1)/n^n) * h_n(S) <= e * (n+1) * h_n(S), for every bounded linear operator between normed spaces over the reals or the complex numbers. Hence, the same factor bounds the gap between any two s-number  sequences. The linear growth in n is order-optimal.  This is the main result of arXiv:2608.05024 and solves a problem of  Mityagin, Henkin (1963) and Carl, Pietsch (1978), up to a constant.
entries.title: The maximal difference theorem for s-numbers

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of the companion paper of the same name (doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.10727.82081). Fix coprime integers p > q ≥ 2 and an integer x₀ ≥ 1 and iterate the ceiling map of the rational base p/q, xₙ = ⌈p·xₙ₋₁/q⌉, with associated word wₙ = q·xₙ₊₁ − p·xₙ ∈ {0,…,q−1}, the correction that makes p·xₙ divisible by q. Four statements are compared. (A) The word of every such orbit is not P-recursive: it satisfies no nontrivial linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients. (B) At p/q = 3/2 the orbit itself is not P-recursive either; for x₀ = 1 it is the sequence A061419, which is therefore not holonomic. (C, D) neither generating function, Σⱼ wⱼzʲ nor Σₙ xₙzⁿ, is algebraic over ℚ(z). The Lean contains a proof of Stanley's algebraic-holonomic-p-recursive closure theorem.
entries.title: Ceiling orbits of rational bases are not P-recursive

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative stability theorem for the one-block endpoint-pullback operator of the shortcut Collatz map. If an arbitrary target set has at most C N^(1-D) exceptions among the positive integers up to N, then, for every central Renyi order 1/2 < theta < 1, every admissible fixed central window, and every positive transport coefficient below the explicit asymptotic slope, its pullback through one floor(log_2 n)-step endpoint is (K(1+C^(theta/(1+theta)))D^(-theta/(2(1+theta))), transport*D)-dense whenever D is sufficiently small. The cutoff and K depend only on the fixed moment and transport parameters, not on the target set or C,D.
entries.title: Refined Arbitrary-Target Transport Through Collatz Endpoints

entries.abstract: Existence of a dimension-independent Hlawka constant for every Schatten p-norm with 1 < p < infinity, and proof that no such constant exists at either endpoint (trace norm at p=1, operator norm at p=infinity).
entries.title: Dimension-independent Hlawka constants for Schatten norms

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the lower bound non(M) ≤ rr, where non(M) is the least cardinality of a nonmeagre subset of the usual real line and rr is the least cardinality of a family of permutations of the natural numbers that changes the sum or destroys convergence of every conditionally convergent real series. It accompanies the manuscript *Determining the Rearrangement Number* by Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues. The reverse inequality was already known in the literature. The reverse inequality, the full equality, and further manuscript corollaries are not formalized in this project.
entries.title: The rearrangement number: non(M) ≤ rr

entries.abstract: General integer-trade criterion and full-factor Cartesian-product kernel/recovery theorem; the all-order grid lower bound; and, for every n ≥ 6, the complete four-parameter integer grid kernel, exact threshold n−2 for odd n and n−3 for even n, optimal n−2 sensor count throughout 2 ≤ h < threshold, and unique four-parameter description of equal-observation populations.
entries.title: Distance-shell tomography: product kernels and sharp grid sensing

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture (2007) and of the matrix theorems that prove it. Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ..., m edges and clique number omega(G). The conjecture states that every noncomplete graph on at least two vertices satisfies lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2 <= 2 (1 - 1/omega(G)) m. The formalization proves it (BN.lambda1_sq_add_lambda2_sq_le) as a consequence of a weighted spectral inequality: for every symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrix B with zero diagonal supported on the edges of G, the sum F(B) of the squares of the two largest positive eigenvalues of B is at most (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||B||_F^2 (BN.weighted). The weighted inequality rests on a complete-positivity theorem for planar Gram matrices: if z_1, ..., z_n in R^2 lie in a closed half-plane through the origin and X is their Gram matrix, then M(X) = X o X + sum over i < j with X_ij < 0 of X_ij^2 (e_i - e_j)(e_i - e_j)^T is completely positive (BN.matrix_theorem), proved by an ordered elimination, a Schur complement identified as a weighted Laplacian plus a matrix with an explicit three-column nonnegative factorization, and total nonnegativity of two rectangular kernels. A variational argument then removes the half-plane hypothesis from the scalar inequality: for every real positive semidefinite X of rank at most two, sum_{i,j} (A_G)_ij (X_ij)_+^2 <= (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||X||_F^2 (BN.gram_le), which also identifies the rank-two conic parameter chi''_{vec,3}(G) of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang with omega(G) (BN.chiVec3_eq_cliqueNum), settling their Conjectures 2 and 3 without a lower bound on the clique number. Previously the conjecture was known for weakly perfect graphs (Ando–Lin), triangle-free graphs (Lin–Ning–Wu), regular graphs (Zhang), graphs with few triangles (Kumar–Pragada, Zeng–Zhang), asymptotically almost surely for random graphs (Liu–Bu), and with weaker constants for all graphs (Coutinho–Spier–Zhang). All five headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: A proof of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture in Lean

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a rerandomized SRHT subspace embedding theorem. For every ambient Walsh dimension n = 2^m, rank 1 <= r <= n, and 0 < epsilon < 1, one deterministic width k <= min(n, ceil(C r / epsilon^2)) can be chosen independently of the orthonormal frame. For each fixed frame, the transform with two independent uniform sign layers and an independent uniform k-subset has spectral failure probability at most 1/100, and preserves all squared norms in that subspace within 1 +/- epsilon with probability at least 99/100. C is an explicit universal constant, with no sharp numerical value claimed. The Comparator selects the spectral theorem and its fixed-frame squared-norm consequence. The full repository retains the 12 named v6 results and their supporting proofs and correspondence maps.
entries.title: Subspace embeddings with the rerandomized SRHT

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Marton's conjecture, widely known as the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, together with its principal consequences. If A is a non-empty subset of an abelian group of exponent 2 with |A + A| <= K|A|, then A is covered by fewer than 2K^12 cosets of a subgroup of cardinality at most |A|; the same conclusion holds with 2K^9 cosets. For an abelian group in which mx = 0 for every x, with m >= 2, the covering number is m * K^(256m^3 + 1). Three consequences are also recorded: a finite set of small doubling in Z^D has a subset of at least K^(-34) of its size whose affine dimension is at most (80/log 2) log K; a map between finite groups of exponent 2 whose additive defects f(x+y) - f(x) - f(y) all lie in a set S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values; and a map that is additive on at least a proportion 1/K of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1)/2 points. The proofs are by an entropy method: one minimizes a functional of the entropic Ruzsa distance between two random variables and shows the minimum is attained at a uniform distribution on a subgroup, so the development also builds a substantial theory of Shannon entropy, entropic Ruzsa distance, and, for the bounded torsion case, a multidistance for m-tuples. The repository is a collaborative formalization project begun in November 2023; the mathematics is due to the cited papers and nothing here is claimed to be new. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the six deliberate holes in PFRPalomar/Challenge.lean.
entries.title: Marton's conjecture (the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the density Hales–Jewett theorem: for every finite alphabet α and every density δ > 0, all sufficiently large n have the property that any set of at least δ·|α|^n words of length n over α contains a combinatorial line. The basis for the formalization is the combinatorial proof of Dodos, Kanellopoulos, and Tyros. As a consequence, we also formalize Szemerédi's theorem on the integers: for every k ≥ 3 and δ > 0, the following holds for all sufficiently large n. Any subset of {0, …, n−1} of size at least δ·n contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k.
entries.title: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and Szemerédi's theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four strengthened almost-all results for shortcut and raw Collatz orbits in ordinary natural density: critical polylogarithmic descent with arbitrary positive divergent target and height multipliers, centered trajectory tubes, and actual first-passage clocks; the fixed-exponent common-landing theorem with the exact upper exceptional-rate endpoint; an explicit reciprocal-order lower bound forced by the joint height ceiling; and a quantitative stretched-logarithmic common-landing theorem with smaller relative-height ceilings. These are almost-all statements and do not prove pointwise Collatz convergence.
entries.title: Polylogarithmic Descent for Almost All Collatz Orbits in Natural Density

entries.abstract: Proves the orthonormal double contraction of the actual corrected curvature derivative of a tangent connection on a smooth finite-dimensional real manifold. The Challenge exposes the corrected commutator and the smooth tangent-vector extensions explicitly; the Solution proves the identity for every supplied extension satisfying the stated hypotheses. The derivative symmetries and cyclic Bianchi equations are derived from torsion-freeness and metric compatibility, not assumed as abstract tensor data. No separate Einstein-divergence theorem is selected.

authors.name: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

entries.title: Double-contracted second Bianchi identity for metric-compatible torsion-free connections

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.
entries.title: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Stein's spherical maximal theorem and Bourgain's circular maximal theorem. The result concerns the sharp range of Lp boundedness of spherical maximal functions in Euclidean space and was first proved by Stein in dimensions three and greater. The much more subtle two-dimensional theorem was first proved by Bourgain. The proof of Bourgain's theorem in this formalization is via Mockenhaupt-Seeger-Sogge's classical argument via a local smoothing estimate for the wave equation. This required first  formalizing various underlying standard results from harmonic analysis. The final theorem statements were written by hand,  while the proofs were almost entirely machine-generated by coding agents with human supervision.
entries.title: Spherical maximal functions: theorems of Stein and Bourgain

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of criteria for Bugeaud's Problem 10.61 ([Bug12, p. 222], due to Mendès France [MF67]): for a Pisot number α > 2 and the Cantor set C(α) = {(α−1) Σ_{k≥1} ε_k α^{−k} : ε_k ∈ {0,1}}, no ξ ∈ C(α) has (ξαⁿ)_{n≥1} uniformly distributed modulo one. The problem is open; what is proved here are criteria for it and two instances. Every compared statement that concludes Problem 10.61 does so for a *quadratic* setup — a real root α > 1 of X² − aX − b whose conjugate has modulus below one — and the two instances are quadratic; the arbitrary-degree material is conditional ingredients, from which no compared statement derives non-equidistribution. Seventeen statements are compared, in four groups. (A) The reduction to symbolic dynamics is an equivalence, and it is complete. (i) Some ξ ∈ C(α) is u.d. mod 1 iff the full two-shift {0,1}^ℤ carries a shift-invariant Borel probability measure whose push-forward under an explicit factor map F is Lebesgue measure on 𝕋. (ii) 10.61 holds at α iff a finite certificate witnesses it: a mean-zero real trigonometric polynomial G on 𝕋 and a c > 0 with ∫ G∘F dμ ≥ c for every invariant μ. (iii) The pressure bracket that makes such a search terminate, −c/β ≤ ∫ g dμ over every invariant μ whenever the pressure of −βg relative to a finite partition is at most c. (B) A pressure criterion. (ii) A bounded measurable potential annihilated by every counterexample measure, an entropy floor h_min for those measures, and a partition pressure below h_min together prove 10.61 at α; and its machine form, where the potential carries a finite-state transfer bound with an integer vector certificate, the hypothesis comparing the log of the certificate ratio, less the Lebesgue mean, against h_min. (iv) The budget identity A(α)·h_min(α) = log 2, tying the Route A exponent to the floor. (C) A covering criterion for quadratic setups, and arbitrary-degree ingredients. (i) Two real inequalities — the depth slope 1 + L/R − L is negative exactly when (L−1)(R−1) > 1, and at the balanced depth M′ = ⌈M·L/R⌉ the covering total obeys an explicit logarithmic bound linear in M with that slope — and then, for a quadratic setup, a numeric certificate at depths (M, M′) yielding one open interval J ⊆ (0,1), uniform in ξ and in n, that every orbit misses at every time, whence A(α) < 1 implies 10.61 at α. (ii) For a quadratic setup of norm −b, the criterion applies exactly when (log₂ α − 1)(log₂(α/|b|) − 1) > 1. This characterizes when A(α) < 1; it does not decide Problem 10.61 for quadratic α with A(α) ≥ 1, about which nothing is compared. (iii) Three ingredients about the family Xᵈ − aXᵈ⁻¹ − 1, valid at every degree d ≥ 2: for a ≥ 3 the real root exceeding a is a Pisot number; every other conjugate has modulus at most (2/a)^{1/(d−1)}; and the numerical inequality log 2/log α + log 2/log(1/ρ) < 1 holds whenever a ≥ 2^{d+1}, a < α, ρ > 0 and a·ρᵈ⁻¹ ≤ 2. These are ingredients, not a criterion: no compared statement carries them to Problem 10.61 above degree two, because (i) is proved only for quadratic setups. At degree two the family members are quadratic setups, and the first of them is α = 2+√5. (D) The two numbers at which the machinery is run to a conclusion, both quadratic: at α = 2+√5 the strong form — an explicit interval missed by every orbit at every time — and 10.61 itself; and at α = 2+√3, 10.61 by a confinement-gap certificate. The informal account is the repository's paper.pdf: machine-written notes documenting the Lean development, not a prior paper that the development formalizes. Credit in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematics and the Lean text are the agents' work, the Fable-5 agent having written the notes and the Opus-5 agent the formalization, each directed turn by turn by Ralf Stephan, who chose the targets, selected which outputs to keep, and releases the files. He does not endorse the informal arguments and has not independently verified informal-to-formal fidelity; where the prose disagrees with the challenge file, the challenge file wins. Every compared statement depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and nothing else.
entries.title: Lean formalization toward Bugeaud Problem 10.61

entries.abstract: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.
entries.title: elliotglazer/erdos501

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp power saving in the finite-field Nikodym problem. A set N in F_q^d is a Nikodym set if through every point x there is a line all of whose points other than x lie in N. Lower bound: for every finite field F_q, every d >= 2 and every Nikodym set N in F_q^d, |N| >= q^d - (8 d^2 + 1) q^(d - 2^(1-d)); the proof goes through a carrier theorem for integral projective varieties containing many affine lines with private points, proved by finite-grid Hermite interpolation, Hilbert-function estimates (normalized monotonicity and a degree upper bound via linear Noether normalization), an interpolation cut, and a dimension induction that halves the saving at each step. Upper bound: for every d >= 2 and epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large primes q there is a Nikodym set N in F_q^d with |N| <= q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) - epsilon), constructed as the complement of a product set built from a totally real multiquadratic order in which q splits completely, with a digit encoding and tangent lines. Together these give Nik(d, q) = q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) + o(1)) along primes. Previously, for general q and d >= 3, the best lower bound was q^d / 2^(d-1) + O(q^(d-1)) and even Nik(d,q) = (1 - o(1)) q^d was open (Lund-Saraf-Wolf, Conjecture 2), while the best upper bounds for prime q were q^d - Omega_d(q^(d - eps_d)) with eps_d << 1/log log d and q^3 - Omega(q^2.1167) (Hunter-Pohoata-Verstraete-Zhang 2026); the lower bound here settles the former conjecture for every finite field, and the construction shows that the exponent d - 1/d conjectured by Chao and Yu (2026) is not sharp over prime fields. The README gives theorem-level comparisons and references. All three headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The sharp finite-field Nikodym exponent

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which answers a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 3 asks whether √3 lies in 𝒮 or in 𝒵. This formalization settles that question and the whole square-root slice: √3 ∈ 𝒵 by an explicit ξ = 1.34160899796…, and for an integer m ≥ 2 one has √m ∈ 𝒮 exactly when m = 2. The cells √5, √6, √7, √8 put four explicit points of 𝒵 in the interval (2,3), the only interval where an answer to Dubickas's Problem 5 could live; they are formalized (SZ.exists_mem_MahlerZ_Ioo_two_three) but are not separately compared, being subsumed by the compared Theorem B. The mechanism is not Diophantine approximation but the arithmetic of Cantor sets, and rests on the triviality that √m² = m is an integer: splitting n into even and odd values turns the one orbit into two base-m orbits coupled by x + √m y = σ, and a covering induction — Utz's 1951 theorem on the distance set of the Cantor discontinuum at m = 3, proved here for every base and every modulus — solves that equation inside the restricted-digit set. The same machinery at a general modulus gives, for p ≥ 2 and non-square m ≥ 3 in either of two explicit ranges, a real ξ ≠ 0 with p ∣ ⌊ξ√mⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 1, hence integral parts that are composite from some point on; and the greedy's branching shows the witnesses for √3 have cardinality 2^ℵ₀, so all but countably many of them are transcendental. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.32215.43682. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery is the Fable-5 agent's; the formalization is the Fable-5 and Opus-5 agents'; the agents also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the collaboration is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency of the development itself.
entries.title: rwst/Square-Roots

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper on the emptiness theory of the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, at and beyond the window length 1/p. The paper introduces block certificates --- finite integer witnesses, rechecked from scratch by the Lean proof kernel, whose soundness rests on the aperiodicity lemma alone --- and uses them to pass the length-$1/p$ line: $\Zset_{3/2}(1/6,13/24)=\emptyset$ (window length $3/8>1/3$), $\Zset_{3/2}(961/3600,2427/3600)=\emptyset$ (length $733/1800$), and explicit unions of total length up to $17/24$, against $20/39$ in print. The closed-interval union statement of Dubickas is replicated exactly as printed; no $\xi\ne0$ keeps $\|\xi(3/2)^{n}\|<1/5$ for every $n$, with $\|\cdot\|$ the distance to the nearest integer; and thirty windows of length $1/p$ are certified at five bases in the regime $p>q^{2}$ that Dubickas leaves open. There is no sorry anywhere outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and no native_decide: every block certificate is discharged by `c.ok = true := by decide`, i.e. by kernel reduction of integer arithmetic on the certificate's raw data.
entries.title: rwst/Confinement-Certificates

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Dmitrii Zakharov's Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem. For every fixed positive dimension d, as p tends to infinity through the primes, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant s(F_p^d) satisfies s(F_p^d) = p w(F_p^d) + o(p), where w is the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.  Supporting proofs include the convex-flag Helly and centerpoint theorems, flag decomposition lemma, balanced convex combinations, relative set expansion, and the polynomial method bound for w. This submission covers Theorem 1.2 and its upper-bound formulation, not every result in the paper. The submission was prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 / 6 Sol-Ultra under the direction and review of the author.  The GitHub page includes a PDF file zakharov_2026-3.pdf containing a revised version of the published paper generated  by ChatGPT 5.6 during this formalization project.  The only noteworthy difference is a correction to Definition 4.6 (Proper points) which was meant to use the function f^circ(q) in  place of \hat f(q) in the published version (this typo slipped in during one of the revision rounds of the paper). No other significant mistakes or corrections were discovered.
entries.title: Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem: Theorem 1.2

entries.abstract: This project formalizes the global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4: every finite abelian extension of the rational numbers embeds into a cyclotomic field. For a number field L that is abelian Galois over the rationals, the selected declaration gives a positive integer n and a rational algebra embedding from L into CyclotomicField n ℚ. The proof is supplied by the ClassFieldTheory library at a fixed commit, using Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib.
entries.title: The global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Li's criterion for the Riemann zeta function, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` holds if and only if every Li-Keiper coefficient of the completed xi function has nonnegative real part. The zero-indexed analytic coefficient at n is Li's classical lambda_(n+1), the n-th Taylor coefficient at 0 of the logarithmic derivative of s |-> xi(1/(1-s)). A second compared theorem identifies this analytic coefficient with Li's arithmetic coefficient, the symmetrized sum over the nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, and proves that symmetrized family summable so the sum is the genuine one. Both results are unconditional: the biconditional, the coefficient identification, the genus-1 Hadamard factorization of xi (with multiplicity), genus-1 summability of 1/|rho|^2, and the growth bound order(xi) <= 1 are all proved. This is a formalization of a classically known equivalence (X.-J. Li, 1997); it is not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nor of the positivity of the coefficients.
entries.title: Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis

entries.abstract: The quality parameter t of a base-2 digital net with 2^m points measures exact equidistribution in dyadic boxes, and for Sobol' sequences used in quasi-Monte Carlo integration and computer graphics the quality of low-dimensional projections is a practical bottleneck. The OneTwo construction of Bonneel, Coeurjolly, Iehl, and Ostromoukhov (ACM Transactions on Graphics, 2025) releases a 692-dimension direction-number table whose protected pairs (2k-1, 2k) have the (1,2) property, with acceptance targets t <= 3 through m <= 10 and t <= 4 through m <= 15 for the pair-aligned four-dimensional blocks. Theorem 1.1 of the preprint determines the next depth exactly: at m = 16, a complete batch of 65,536 points, every one of the 345 pair-aligned windows of the released table has exact four-dimensional t-value 4 when its first dimension is one of 1, 7, 31, 49, 67, 195, 225, 243, 373 and t-value 5 otherwise, so the t <= 4 guarantee extends to m = 16 in exactly nine windows and fails in the other 336, each failure witnessed by an empty dyadic box of volume 2^-12 in that projection. The standard star-discrepancy bound for the projection is 299/4096 at t = 4 and 29/256 at t = 5. This Lean development proves the theorem in rank form with the released table embedded as one 256-bit literal per dimension: for every window, every four-part composition at the threshold total selects independent generator rows over F_2 and some composition one total higher does not, and the distribution is 9 windows at t = 4 and 336 at t = 5. The worked block, dimensions 25 to 28, keeps its separate explicit certificate (t = 5, with every smaller threshold refuted). All checks are 16-column XOR row reductions reduced by kernel decide with no native evaluation. The digital-net rank criterion, the discrepancy bound, and the authentication of the upstream table remain informal.
entries.title: Exact four-dimensional projection quality of the OneTwo Sobol' table at 65,536 points

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and mathlib formalization of the Dong-Yang classification of optimal (n,4) binary block codes for binary symmetric channels.  The registered results are Theorems 1-5 of the paper: existence of an optimal linear or Class-I code, the explicit linear optimal codes by residue class modulo 3, the universal strict-improvement reductions outside the linear, Class-I, and Class-II classes, the Class-I condition reduction to linear codes, and the finite classification for blocklengths 2 <= n <= 8. The Lean statements use the strict-improvement contrapositive forms.
entries.title: N4Code: optimal finite-length block codes of size four for binary symmetric channels

entries.abstract: For every positive integer n, the Euclidean kissing number tau_n is an attained maximum and satisfies tau_n <= (sqrt(6))^n. This Lean formalization proves the bound by packing explicit bodies of revolution in the unit ball, including the geometric separation, volume integrals, and every dimension case. An explicit six-point planar configuration proves tau_2 = 6. Consequently sqrt(6) is the least nonnegative (and least positive) universal exponential base without a prefactor; the admissible bases are exactly alpha >= sqrt(6), and the supremum of tau_n^(1/n) over positive dimensions equals sqrt(6). No asymptotic-optimality claim is made.
entries.title: The optimal universal exponential base for Euclidean kissing numbers

entries.abstract: This repository formalizes Brill--Noether generality for chains whose factors may be cycles or theta graphs, subject to a genericity condition on path lengths and an evenly-marked condition on the theta factors. A graph is called Brill--Noether general if the possible degrees and ranks of its chip configurations, in the sense of Baker and Norine, match the behavior of a general algebraic curve. Here we use only the existential form of Brill--Noether generality, without computing dimensions. Following Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, we also formalize a mild vanishing-order condition that permits the recovery of dimension statements on the algebraic side. A Brill--Noether general graph also has the conjectural maximum gonality in its genus. The chain of cycles case is a theorem of Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, which Pflueger--Solomon generalized to allow evenly-marked theta graphs. Among other things, the construction shows the existence, in every positive genus g, of graphs with every gonality between 2 and ceil(g/2) + 1, inclusive.
entries.title: Brill--Noether generality and gonality for chains of cycles and theta graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture introduced by Claude Carlet. For the derivative image of the Kasami monomial x^(4^k-2^k+1) with gcd(k,n)=1, over a finite field of characteristic two with 2^n elements, the formalized result gives the exact three-variable coefficient count 2^(2n-3) for every pair of distinct nonzero coefficients.
entries.title: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture

entries.abstract: Sixteen compared statements establish quantitative recurrence for the actual infinite Padovan prefix path and compare cubic and quartic arithmetic record windows. For 0<epsilon<=1, every nonempty prefix whose conjugate coordinate lies within epsilon of the origin has expanding coordinate at least epsilon^(-2); an actual prefix returns with expanding coordinate at most r^3*epsilon^(-2). Every letter stream satisfies the pairwise bound abs(Delta X)*norm(Delta W)^2>=1, and Padovan substitution stages attain equality at arbitrarily large clocks. The full cubic record window is relatively dense with uniformly discrete differences; the identical positive-real window in the quartic case admits nonzero inverse-unit points arbitrarily close to zero, while its other real embedding grows. Scalar prefix coordinates factor the included faithful chiral timelike history in the genuine quartic trace geometry. The formalization exposes the return bounds, actual-word attainment, constructive covering, and explicit obstruction as its principal mathematical consequences.
entries.title: Sharp arithmetic separation in chiral Padovan histories

entries.abstract:
Erdős Problem 647 asks whether there is any n > 24 with max_{m < n} (m + tau(m)) <= n + 2, where tau counts divisors. The value n = 24 satisfies it and the question is open. This entry certifies a bounded exclusion: no such n exists in (24, 10^8]. It does not resolve the problem and asserts nothing about n > 10^8.
The exclusion is certified rather than searched at check time. A witness at a cover position is an offset together with prime-power pairs dividing m, certifying tau(m) >= prod (e + 1); every prime in a pair is below 1024 and is checked prime by eleven trial divisions, so no primality certificates appear anywhere. A chain of witnesses covers the interval and each certificate chunk is discharged by a single decide against the chain checker, so the Lean kernel certifies the arithmetic and the generator that produced it is never trusted.
The audience is the community working on the Erdős problems database and its Lean formalizations, for whom a machine-checked lower bound on the search range is directly usable, and researchers building certificate-based exclusions in elementary number theory, for whom the witness format and its kernel-evaluable checkers are the transferable part.
entries.title: A kernel-checked exclusion certificate for Erdős Problem 647, to 10^8

entries.abstract: Alexa's three-dimensional Tutte embedding theorem (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2025) requires the graph of a tetrahedral mesh to have neither a K₆ nor a K₃,₃,₁ minor and asks whether the second exclusion is necessary. The paper proves that it is redundant for finite simplicial complexes whose realization is a closed topological 3-ball and which satisfy the boundary-triangle condition (BT): if the 1-skeleton G has no K₆ minor, then G is linklessly embeddable and hence has no K₃,₃,₁ minor (Theorem 1.1). This Lean development proves the paper's new combinatorial mathematics over mathlib simple graphs and finite simplicial complexes and composes it into Theorem 1.1 with the cited theorems as explicit hypotheses. Proved: for every four-clique of a (BT) pair the induced relative F₂ chain complex has homology of dimension at most one (Lemma 4.3, with the soundness of its Boolean coordinate model, Lemma 7.1); a K₄-attachment never merges components of the old part (Lemma 5.2); every MP₁-cockade whose four-clique deletions leave at most two components is linklessly embeddable, given the four-clique Holst–Lovász–Schrijver criterion and linkless atoms (Proposition 5.3); and the joined statement structural_theorem, in which the skeleton of the complex is a mathlib SimpleGraph, every skeleton four-clique is a labelled four-clique of the pair, and the hypotheses are Corollary 3.6 (rigidity, Mader, Jørgensen), the relative ball duality of Section 4, Corollary 2.5, and Lemma 5.1. Generic rigidity, the extremal-minor classification, PL duality, the Holst–Lovász–Schrijver theorem, apex linklessness, and Alexa's theorem are not formalized and enter only as named hypotheses.
entries.title: Combinatorial core of the K₃,₃,₁-redundancy theorem for tetrahedral balls

entries.abstract: This Lean development proves that the even-order permutation construction of Grünschloß and Keller (MCQMC 2008 proceedings, implemented in gendiag0m2.h) is a base-2 (0,m,2)-net for every even m >= 4. The proof is symbolic: for every resolution a <= m the dyadic-box map is shown injective through the concatenation x = floor(k/4) + 2^(m/2-2) z and fixed-width bit-reversal splitting, and a cardinality argument upgrades injectivity to a bijection (exactly one point per elementary interval). For the source's row-shifted tiling lattice <(N,0),(N/4,N)> it proves, for every even m >= 8, that one explicit pair of points has squared distance 241 * 2^(m-8), and at m = 8 that 241 is the exact minimum over all pairs and all lattice translates. The exhaustive m = 8 lower bound is reduced by ordinary kernel decide; the exactness of the computed candidate minimum over the whole lattice is a symbolic lemma. The all-parameter lower bound of the distance theorem (even m >= 10) is proved in the paper but is not formalized.
entries.title: Even-order Grünschloß–Keller permutation nets: net property and tiling distance

entries.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tucker's Lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) and the combinatorial Borsuk–Ulam theorem in 1D and 2D without artificial conditions. Formalizes four foundational pillars: (1) 1D discrete sign-change parity and antipodal interval subdivision lemma; (2) 2D combinatorial double counting of face doors and modulo-2 parity conservation on edge-pseudomanifolds; (3) the boundary cycle engine on 2D edge-pseudomanifolds with an enumerated cyclic boundary (CyclicBoundaryPseudomanifold2D) under antipodal boundary labeling, proving that non-complementary boundary labelings force odd boundary door parity, thereby establishing the 2D Tucker's Lemma on cyclic boundary pseudomanifolds, retracting previous claims of full topological disk coverage; and (4) the concrete 6-vertex, 8-face, 12-edge octahedral 2-sphere S^2_8 triangulation. All declarations rely strictly on standard Lean 4 kernel axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice).
entries.title: Tucker's Lemma: Full Combinatorial & Topological Parity Suite in 1D and 2D

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the main theorem of J. H. Bae, "Unbounded logarithmic limsup in Erdős Problem 684 via shifted carry scheduling" (arXiv:2604.23784, v3).  For 0 ≤ k ≤ n write C(n,k) = u·v with u supported on the primes ≤ k and v on the primes in (k,n], and let f(n) be the least k with u > n²; Erdős asked for bounds on f(n) (Problem 684 in Bloom's database).  The compared theorems state that for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many n with f(n) > (1/2 − ε)·log n·log log n / log log log n, equivalently limsup f(n)·log log log n /(log n·log log n) ≥ 1/2 (stated in the extended nonnegative reals), and in particular that f(n)/log n is unbounded, so no estimate f(n) = O(log n) holds.  This strengthens the subsequential lower bound (1/2 − o(1)) log n of Alexeev–Putterman–Sawhney–Sellke–Valiant by a factor of order log log n / log log log n; the general upper bound (log n)² remains the best known and the exact order of f(n) is open.  Two further compared statements fix the meaning of the definitions: u(n,k) times the part of C(n,k) supported on primes exceeding k equals C(n,k), and K < f(n) holds exactly when u(n,k) ≤ n² for all 1 ≤ k ≤ min(K,n).  The proof follows the paper section by section (Kummer carries, a product-cell code, a CRT count with exponential weighting, an anchored-fibre selection lemma, and a four-range carry budget).  The prime number theorem is the single analytic input: the library proves the theorem under the explicit hypothesis θ(x) = x + O(x/log² x) and then discharges that hypothesis from the bound ψ(x) = x + O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/10})) of the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project (Kontorovich, Tao et al.), so the compared theorems carry no hypotheses and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 684: f(n)/log n is unbounded — a Lean 4 formalization of arXiv:2604.23784

entries.abstract: Let H be a subgroup of a finite group G, let n = [G:H] > 1, and let p be the least prime divisor of n. This Lean development proves an exact finite rational upper envelope for the number of subgroups K with H ≤ K ≤ G and the strict bound c(p) n^((log_p n)/4), where c(p) is an Euler-product times a Gaussian theta series. It formalizes the bandwise moment inequality that drives the proof, a universal base-two bound with an exact decimal coefficient, the exact optimal answer for prime-power indices, and elementary-abelian asymptotics showing that both the constant and the exponent 1/4 are optimal.
entries.title: Sharp bounds for intervals in finite subgroup lattices
